s1.syndrome_frame: Exertional chest pain with transient ECG changes
salient_findings: Left bundle-branch block (LBBB) during stress test
key_facts: Patient in their early 60s
2-week history of chest pain during exertion
Chest pain consistently presented during physical activity
Patient is a nonsmoker
No family history of premature coronary artery disease
Baseline 12-lead ECG showed no substantial abnormalities
Stress ECG developed LBBB in stage 2 at heart rate of 107 beats per minute
LBBB resolved following exercise cessation with immediate angina relief
No ischemic or memory T waves in pre- and post-exercise ECGs
Coronary computed tomography angiography showed no abnormalities

shortlist.label: Coronary artery spasm
shortlist.why_kept: Exertional chest pain with transient ECG changes, consistent with coronary artery spasm

shortlist.label: Prinzmetal's angina
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain during exertion with transient ECG changes, similar to Prinzmetal's angina

shortlist.label: Myocardial bridge
shortlist.why_kept: Exertional chest pain with transient ECG changes, possible myocardial bridge

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain during exertion, possible hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

shortlist.label: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain during exertion, possible atherosclerotic coronary artery disease despite negative coronary computed tomography angiography

raw.rationale: The patient's chest pain during exertion, development of LBBB during stress ECG that resolved with exercise cessation, and immediate angina relief without evidence of ischemic changes or coronary artery disease on CT angiography, are consistent with coronary artery spasm.

rejected.label: Prinzmetal's angina
rejected.why: While similar, Prinzmetal's angina typically occurs at rest and is associated with transient ST-segment elevation, which was not observed in this case.

rejected.label: Myocardial bridge
rejected.why: Myocardial bridge is a possible cause of chest pain, but the lack of specific findings on coronary CT angiography and the nature of the symptoms make it less likely.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of hypertrophy on the ECG or other diagnostic tests, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease
rejected.why: The coronary computed tomography angiography showed no abnormalities, which contradicts the typical findings of atherosclerotic coronary artery disease.
